title: Rigorous Low-Degree Implications for Planted Subgraph Detection: Noise and Treewidth
summary: The low-degree heuristic has become a widely used framework for predicting computational thresholds in average-case planted-versus-null problems. However, a recent sequence of counterexamples shows that low-degree indistinguishability does not, in general, rule out efficient noise-tolerant distinguishers; see Buhai et al. (2025) and Mao (2026). Motivated by these developments, Hsieh et al. (2026) initiated the study of rigorous consequences of the low-degree heuristic.
